title: Red beans and rice
subtitle: Monday-night New Orleans pot of kidney beans with andouille
excerpt: Red beans and rice is a New Orleans Monday-night tradition: dried red kidney beans simmered for hours with smoked sausage, the Cajun trinity, and bay leaves until the beans are creamy and the liquid has thickened to a gravy. Served over long-grain rice. Simple, deeply satisfying, almost entirely hands-off after the first ten minutes.
sourceNotes: New Orleans culinary tradition. Red beans and rice on Monday is said to derive from the tradition of washing clothes on Monday while the beans cooked unattended on the hob. Documented in WPA Louisiana Writers' Project food surveys and Paul Prudhomme, Chef Paul Prudhomme's Louisiana Kitchen (1984).

recipe.freezeNotes: The beans freeze well for up to 3 months. Freeze without the rice.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make entirely ahead and reheat. The flavour improves significantly the next day.

content.text: Red beans and rice is dried kidney beans soaked overnight then simmered for 2 to 3 hours with smoked sausage, onion, celery, green pepper, garlic, and bay. The beans soften and the starch thickens the liquid to a gravy. The dish is almost entirely hands-off after the first ten minutes.

items.prepNote: dried, soaked overnight in cold water

content.text: Drain and rinse the soaked {{kidney-beans}} of kidney beans. Heat {{vegetable-oil}} of oil in the Dutch oven over medium heat. Brown the {{smoked-pork-sausage}} of sausage slices for 3 minutes. Remove and set aside. Add the {{onion}} onion, {{celery}} celery, and {{pepper-green}} green pepper. Cook for 5 minutes. Add {{garlic}} of garlic, {{cayenne-pepper}} of cayenne, {{paprika-smoked}} of smoked paprika, and {{thyme-dried}} of thyme. Cook for 1 minute.

Add the drained beans, {{bay-leaves}} of bay, the browned sausage, and enough water to cover by 5 cm. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a steady simmer. Cook uncovered for 2 to 2.5 hours, stirring occasionally.

When the beans are completely tender, scoop out about a third of them into a bowl and mash roughly with a fork. Return to the pot and stir through: this thickens the sauce without any starch. Season with salt. Serve over long-grain rice with spring onions and hot sauce.

items.fix: Old dried beans take longer. Add a little more water and keep simmering. Do not add salt until the beans are tender: salt added early toughens the skins.

items.cause: Too much water, or beans not mashed.
items.fix: Mash a third of the beans as described and stir back in. This is the traditional thickening method.
Taste before serving and adjust salt, cayenne, and hot sauce. The dish needs assertive seasoning.

content.text: A vegetarian version replaces the sausage with smoked paprika, a teaspoon of chipotle paste, and a large mushroom cut into thick slices. The dish works with tinned kidney beans for a faster weeknight version: reduce the simmering time to 30 minutes. Pinto beans or black beans can be substituted.

Red beans and rice on a Monday is one of New Orleans' most cherished food traditions. Monday was washing day: the hob was tied up with laundry, but the beans could be left to simmer all morning. Electric washing machines made the original reason obsolete. The dish stayed anyway, because it is too good to give up.
